study_identification_part.si_4_title: Structural variability of the cerebral cortex in schizophrenia and its association with clinical symptoms

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used the person-based similarity index (PBSI) to estimate the global variation in cortical measures within the same group. PBSI was calculated by correlating each individual's cortical structural profile with all other individuals within the same group using Spearman's correlation coefficient rho, then averaging the n-1 correlation coefficients per participant. Z-scores of PBSI were calculated using the mean and SD of healthy controls to divide patients into 'deviant' and 'other patients' groups (criterion: lower than mean - 1.5 SD).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We calculated the PBSI scores to estimate the global variation in cortical measures within the same group. Following a procedure validated in previous studies, the PBSI score for the cortical measure was calculated within the same group. [...] In the patient group, we calculated the z score of the PBSI score using the mean and S.D. of the PBSI scores in the control group. Using the z score of the PBSI score, we divided the patient group into 'deviant' and 'other patients' based on a criterion of lower than the mean -1.5 S.D.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Four morphometric features across 308 cortical structures were calculated: surface area (SA), gray matter volume (GMV), cortical thickness (CT), and local gyrification index (LGI). PBSI scores were calculated for each measure separately (PBSI-SA, PBSI-GV, PBSI-CT, PBSI-LGI) and for all measures combined (PBSI-All). The 308 cortical regions were derived from a subdivision of the Desikan-Killiany atlas.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Four morphometric features across 308 cortical structures were calculated: surface area, gray matter volume, thickness, and local gyrification index.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: ComBat harmonization was performed to adjust for site differences with age, sex, and diagnosis as covariates. The normative modeling approach used z-scores calculated from healthy control group statistics (mean and SD of PBSI scores) to identify deviant patients. Age and sex were matched between groups, and site effects were adjusted through harmonization.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: We performed ComBat harmonization to adjust for the variation generated from the use of different neuroimaging datasets with the covariates of age, sex, and diagnosis.
